summary: Discovery call with HarborView Bank focusing on data residency, HIPAA/GDPR implications, and tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Customer wants evidence of SOC2 and encryption-at-rest, strict logging redaction, and options for on-prem/VPC deployment. Agreed next steps include sending security docs, scheduling technical deep-dive, and scoping a pilot for limited internal apps.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs
audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC and monitoring
transcript:
[00:00] Sophia Ramirez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sophia from Redwood, with Ethan our SE. How are you all?
[00:12] Lisa Chang: Good, thanks. We just wanted to get into the data residency and compliance part, we have some strict regs across EU and US.
[00:25] Ethan Cole: Great, can you give a quick rundown of your current stack and where data lives today?
[00:35] Tom Reyes: Sure, so most of our customer data lives in AWS us-east-1, we have a EU region for EU customers in eu-west-1, all PII lives in our vault and we use a customer-managed KMS. We are evaluating options to host inference, we're worried about logs and token storage, like where are chat logs stored, retention and ability to redact.
[01:05] Priya Malhotra: Right, and from compliance we'd need HIPAA guard rails for any PHI - even though we're a bank, sometimes we process health-related claims for some clients, and GDPR for EU customers - data residency and ability to delete.
[01:25] Sophia Ramirez: Totally, that's pretty common. Quick overview: Redwood Hosted keeps data in our managed infra but we have region pins and options for data residency in specific regions. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity with customer isolation, and Private gives you a customer-controlled control plane in your VPC or on-prem. Each has different controls around keys, logs, and audit.
[01:50] Ethan Cole: From a security perspective, for Private we can support customer-managed KMS/HSM and VPC peering so keys never leave your environment; for Dedicated we offer strong isolation but keys are usually customer-provided via KMS integrations, and Hosted uses our managed KMS unless you bring your own in certain enterprise configs.
[02:15] Lisa Chang: When you say "logs" — do you persist request transcripts? We need strict logging restrictions and redaction, even to prevent any PHI from being stored in audit logs.
[02:30] Ethan Cole: Good question. By default we do collect telemetry for debugging and usage, but for enterprise we can disable transcript persistence and only persist structured metadata. We also support configurable retention windows and an automatic PII redaction pipeline. Note: redaction isn't 100% perfect in auto mode, so many customers choose Private or Dedicated + strict retention for PHI workloads.
[02:58] Tom Reyes: That was my concern, also tokenization, KV cache. If we do caching for performance, where is the KV cache stored? Could it leak across tenants?
[03:12] Sophia Ramirez: The KV cache is per-model per-deployment. For Hosted it's multi-tenant but logically isolated; for Dedicated and Private it's exclusive to your pool. We can also disable KV cache if you prefer lower attack surface, though it affects latency and cost.
[03:32] Lisa Chang: Okay. Also audit logs — we need immutable audit logs that we can ingest into our SIEM.
[03:40] Ethan Cole: We export audit logs to S3 or to your SIEM via syslog / SIEM connector. For Private, logs live in your environment so you control retention and immutability. For Hosted, we provide a managed export and can sign BAA/SLA for retention policies.
[04:00] Priya Malhotra: About GDPR: right to be forgotten — can you remove data for a user on demand, including any cached vectors or embeddings?
[04:10] Sophia Ramirez: Yes, we have deletion APIs that purge input storage and can invalidate KV caches. Embeddings and derived artifacts can be deleted on request. In Hosted there is a process and potential delays; in Private you have immediate control.
[04:30] Tom Reyes: Latency is another tradeoff—if we go Private in our on-prem DC we'll avoid cross-region hops but we need Redwood to support the runtime performance and optimized kernels.
[04:42] Ethan Cole: Absolutely — our runtime supports kernel selection and quantization strategies; in Private you can pin model variants. We usually run a small benchmark during pilot to measure token-per-second and latency.
[04:58] Lisa Chang: Speaking of models, can you commit to not training on our data?
[05:05] Sophia Ramirez: We do not use customer prompts or outputs to train our public models. We have contractual clauses and can put it in the DPA; for Private it's fully customer-controlled.
[05:20] [00:05:25] Tom Reyes: One more thing, SSO & RBAC — we need SAML OKTA integration, SCIM provisioning and fine-grained roles for auditors vs devs.
[05:35] Ethan Cole: We support SAML SSO, SCIM, and role-based access controls. For Private, you can integrate with your central IdP so tokens never traverse our hosted control plane.
[05:50] Lisa Chang: Is there any SOC 2 / ISO documentation we can review before legal signs off?
[05:56] Sophia Ramirez: Yes, we'll share SOC 2 Type II, ISO attestation, penetration test summaries, and a security whitepaper. I'll include that in the follow-up.
[06:10] Priya Malhotra: Regarding HIPAA, do you sign BAAs?
[06:16] Sophia Ramirez: Yes, for customers processing PHI we do execute BAAs. For Hosted we have a standard process; Dedicated and Private have enterprise options.
[06:25] Tom Reyes: For Private, what about networking? Can we do VPC peering or do you support private link?
[06:31] Ethan Cole: We support VPC peering, PrivateLink equivalents, and on-prem connectors. For Private deployments we can run a control plane in your VPC and optionally an air-gapped option.
[06:45] Lisa Chang: There was a comment earlier about automatic fallback & graceful degradation. If our primary region is down, what's the failover pattern?
[06:53] Sophia Ramirez: We have routing policies — you can prefer low-latency region, fallback to other regions or model variants. For critical financial workflows we recommend Dedicated with cross-region standby pools to meet SLA.
[07:05] Tom Reyes: Cost question: can you share a rough hosted vs dedicated vs private unit cost? We're trying to justify a pilot to finance.
[07:14] Sophia Ramirez: We'll send a cost comparison sheet. Hosted has the lowest upfront but higher per-token for heavy usage; Dedicated reduces unit cost with committed capacity; Private has the highest setup but gives full control and compliance alignment. We'll tailor numbers to your expected QPS and sequence lengths.
[07:30] Priya Malhotra: Can we scope a pilot — limited to internal support agent app, only US data, and with transcripts disabled?
[07:38] Sophia Ramirez: Yes, that makes sense as a pilot. Suggested scope: 6-week pilot, 2 models (small and medium) for comparison, data residency in us-east-1, transcripts off, retention 7 days, structured metrics and perf benchmark.
[07:56] Tom Reyes: For the pilot do you need any network access or a POC environment?
[08:02] Ethan Cole: For Hosted pilot no network change; for Dedicated we'll provision a reserved pool; for Private we will need VPC peering details and maybe a VPN. We'll detail options in the follow-up.
[08:20] Lisa Chang: Any gotchas around encryption? We require envelope encryption with customer-managed keys and key rotation policy.
[08:29] Sophia Ramirez: We support envelope encryption and key rotation. In Private your KMS/HSM is fully under your control; in Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS; Hosted supports BYOK in enterpise setups.
[08:45] [00:08:50] Priya Malhotra: Are there examples of other banks using Redwood for similar compliance profiles?
[08:54] Sophia Ramirez: Yes, we'll share anonymized case studies of banks and fintechs who used Dedicated and Private deployments to meet similar regs.
[09:05] Tom Reyes: What about developer experience — we need same API for hosted and private so integrations don't change.
[09:12] Ethan Cole: That's a key Redwood design point: same API surface and SDKs across environments. You pin model versions and rollouts via our console or API.
[09:25] Lisa Chang: On the legal side, we'll need DPA, BAA, and security appendices. Can your legal team provide templated agreements?
[09:33] Sophia Ramirez: Yes, we'll attach standard templates and redline process. Legal typically asks for more info after the security docs.
[09:42] Priya Malhotra: On logging, one more ask: can we redact PII at the ingestion layer so it never enters logs?
[09:49] Ethan Cole: We have pre-ingest redaction hooks — you can run a redactor in your sidecar or request a managed redaction pipeline. For strictest cases, we recommend Private with client-side redaction.
[10:05] Lisa Chang: Great. I think that's the main items. Can we recap next steps?
[10:10] Sophia Ramirez: Sure. Recap: we'll send SOC2/HIPAA docs and security whitepaper, provide a hosted vs private cost comparison tailored to your expected usage, schedule a technical deep-dive next week, and scope a 6-week pilot limited to internal app in us-east-1 with transcripts off.
[10:30] Tom Reyes: I'll send the regulatory controls and list of data zones.
[10:34] Priya Malhotra: I'll confirm PHI presence in the pilot data set by tomorrow.
[10:38] Sophia Ramirez: Perfect. We'll follow up with a calendar invite for the deep-dive. Thanks everyone.
[10:45] Lisa Chang: Thanks, bye.
[41:30] End of recording.

Notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions in product names (e.g., "PrivateLink" vs our internal name), filler words, and speaker overlaps. References to KV cache, KMS, VPC peering, SOC 2, BAA, SAML/SCIM and audit log export were captured for follow up.
